sentences.text: 2. It is submitted that the dispute between the husband and the wife was subsequently settled and reported before this Court in MFA No.675/2025 which arose out of M.C.No.9/2025.

They submit that joint Compromise Petition in MFA No.675/2025, is signed by the parties and their learned counsels and based on the joint Compromise Petition, MFA No.675/2025 was disposed of and NC:
2025:KHC:44679 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER consequently, proceedings in M.C.No.9/2025 was also closed.
3. The Compromise Petition which was filed in MFA No.675/2025 is placed before the Court along with a memo dated 03.11.2025 which is filed by the petitioner in Crl.P.No.3130/2024.
4.

Perusal of the averments found in the joint Compromise Petition filed in MFA No.675/2025 would go to show that the parties have agreed to withdraw Crl.P.No.3856/2022 which arises out of Crime No.69/2022 registered by Thalaghattapura Police Station, Bangalore, Crl.P.No.4955/2022 which arises out of C.C.No.20877/2021 pending before the Court of II ACJM, Bangalore Rural and Crl.P.No.3357/2024 which arises out of Crime No.281/2022 in C.C.No.8472/2024 registered by Wilson Garden Police Station, Bangalore.
5. In paragraph No.6 of the joint Compromise Petition, the agreed terms and conditions between the parties has been extracted.

Paragraph No.6 in the joint NC: 2025:KHC:44679 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER Compromise Petition filed in MFA No.675/2025, reads as under:
"6.

After litigating the above cases, the parties thought over the matter, had consultation with the respective family members and elders the appellant and the respondent No.1 mutually decided to withdraw the cases initiated against each other and settle the disputes between them amicably on the following terms and conditions:
a) The appellant and the 1st respondent agree to dissolve their marriage by mutual consent with each withdrawing the allegations made against the other in M.C.No.5412/2021.
b) The appellant will give up her claims over the arrears of interim maintenance of Rs.65,00,000/- (Rupees Sixty Five Lakh Only) due to her from the 1st respondent.

c) Pursuant to the proceedings in C.C.No.20877/2021 initiated pursuant to the complaint by the appellant, the amount kept in A/c No.063963700000382 maintained at Yes Bank Cunningham Road Branch, at Bengaluru has been frozen.
The appellant has no objection to defreeze the said account.

The Appellant and the Respondent No.1 undertake not to disclose private WhatsApp information, chats, messages, conversations, e-mails, private - 12 -  NC: 2025:KHC:44679  HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER videos, photographs or any other documents in any form relating to each other which may be in their custody.

No coercion, fraud or undue influence has been practiced or exercised by one over the other in getting the consent for entering into this settlement."

6. It is relevant to note that, in paragraph No.6(c), it is mentioned that pursuant to the proceedings in C.C.No.20877/2021 initiated based on the complaint by Smt. Deepali Lengade, the amount kept in account No.063963700000382 maintained at Yes Bank, Cunningham Road Branch, Bangalore by Sri. Sandeep Lengade has been freezed and Smt.Deepali Lengade has no objection to defreeze the said account.

In paragraph No.6(f) of the joint - 13 -  NC: 2025:KHC:44679 HC-KAR AND 1 OTHER Compromise Petition, the parties have agreed to settle the dispute in C.C.No.8472/2024 arising out of Crime No.281/2022 which was initiated on the complaint of Sri.Sandeep Lengade against Smt.Deepali Lengade and her advocates.
7. Accused in C.C.No.8472/2024 are before this Court in Crl.P.No.3130/2024.
In view of the averments found in Clause 6(f) of the joint Compromise Petition, the proceedings in C.C.No.8472/2024 out of which Crl.P.No. 3130/2024 arises needs to be quashed.
